gap_report_metadata.requirement_title: As a customer, I want to browse available mobile devices, review product details and default configurations, view promotional offers and estimated delivery information, authenticate when required, and seamlessly continue my purchase journey after successful login, so that I can make an informed purchase decision and complete my mobile device purchase successfully.

unmapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC7 – Responsive Authentication Popup (Fully Covered)

The application shall ensure that the authentication popup:

Displays correctly on Desktop.
Displays correctly on Tablet.
Displays correctly on Mobile.
Maintains usability across supported screen resolutions.
unmapped_criteria.gap_analysis: No test cases in the retrieved TestRail suite explicitly validate the responsive behavior of the authentication popup across Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile devices or verify usability across different screen resolutions. This acceptance criterion requires dedicated responsive design testing which is not present in the current test suite. This represents a critical gap in cross-platform quality assurance and may result in poor user experience on non-desktop devices.
unmapped_criteria.action_required: Create comprehensive responsive design test cases to validate: (1) Authentication popup displays correctly on Desktop (1920x1080, 1366x768), (2) Authentication popup displays correctly on Tablet (768x1024, 1024x768), (3) Authentication popup displays correctly on Mobile (375x667, 414x896), (4) All popup elements (message, login button, sign-up button) are accessible and usable across all screen resolutions, (5) Popup layout adapts appropriately without overlapping or truncation. Prioritize mobile and tablet testing as these represent significant user traffic for e-commerce applications.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC3 – Default Product Configuration (Partially Covered)

When the Product Details Page is opened, the application shall:

Display the default device colour.
Display the default storage option.
Display the default payment option.
Display the correct pricing for the default configuration.
Display the estimated delivery date.
Display the promotional offer (if available).
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify default device configuration values on Samsung Galaxy A57 5G product detail page
Verify default configuration visibility when PDP loads with delayed hydration
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases 1429 and 1434 validate default colour ('Awesome Navy'), storage ('256 GB'), and payment option ('24-month installment') under normal and delayed loading conditions. However, they do not explicitly verify the correct pricing for the default configuration, estimated delivery date, or promotional offer display, leaving gaps in complete AC3 coverage. Missing pricing validation creates financial risk, while missing delivery date and promotional offer validation impacts customer decision-making and conversion rates.
recommended_test_enhancements: Enhance test case 1429 to add validation steps for: (1) Correct pricing is displayed for the default configuration (Awesome Navy, 256 GB, 24-month installment) with expected price assertion, (2) Estimated delivery date is visible and accurate on the PDP with format validation, (3) Promotional offers are displayed when available and hidden when not applicable with conditional validation logic.

Enhance test case 1434 to add validation steps for pricing, estimated delivery date, and promotional offer display under delayed loading/hydration conditions to ensure these critical elements render correctly even with network latency.
Create dedicated test data sets with expected pricing for all default configuration combinations to enable automated price validation and prevent pricing display errors in production.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC4 – Continue Purchase Journey (Partially Covered)

The customer shall be able to:

View the Next button.
Click the Next button.
Continue to the next purchase step.
Prevent duplicate submissions when the button is clicked multiple times.
Resume the purchase journey after successful authentication.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify Next button initiates progression to next step for authenticated user
Verify Next button behavior when clicked multiple times rapidly by unauthenticated user
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test case 1430 validates Next button visibility, click functionality, and progression to the next step for authenticated users. Test case 1435 validates prevention of duplicate submissions through rapid clicking. However, there is no explicit test case validating that the user can resume the purchase journey after successful authentication (i.e., being redirected back to the interrupted purchase step after login). This gap creates risk of poor user experience where customers lose their configuration selections after authentication, potentially leading to cart abandonment.
recommended_test_enhancements: Enhance test case 1430 to add validation steps: (1) Verify user is on the next step of the purchase journey (e.g., plan selection page), (2) Verify the device configuration selected on the PDP is preserved and displayed on the next step with all user selections intact.

Create a new end-to-end test case to validate the complete authentication flow: (1) Unauthenticated user selects device configuration on PDP, (2) User clicks Next, (3) Login popup appears, (4) User successfully logs in, (5) User is redirected back to the PDP or the next step in the purchase journey with their previous configuration preserved, (6) User can continue the purchase journey without re-selecting options.
Add session state validation to ensure configuration persistence across authentication boundary, including device model, colour, storage, and payment option selections.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC5 – Authentication (Partially Covered)

If the customer is not authenticated, the application shall:

Display the Login popup after clicking Next.
Display Login and Sign Up options.
Prevent the purchase journey until authentication is completed.
Redirect the customer back to the interrupted purchase step after successful login.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify login or sign-up popup is displayed for unauthenticated user clicking Next
Verify authentication popup elements are accessible with timing-sensitive overlay rendering
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases 1431 and 1436 validate that the Login popup is displayed after clicking Next for unauthenticated users, verify the presence of 'Log in with Hub ID' and 'Don't have an account? Sign up here' options, and confirm popup accessibility under delayed rendering conditions. However, they do not explicitly test that the purchase journey is prevented until authentication is completed or that the customer is redirected back to the interrupted purchase step after successful login. This gap creates security risk (unauthorized purchase progression) and user experience risk (lost configuration after login).
recommended_test_enhancements: Enhance test case 1431 to add validation steps: (1) Attempt to bypass authentication and verify purchase journey is blocked, (2) Complete login with valid Hub ID credentials, (3) Verify user is redirected back to the Samsung Galaxy A57 5G PDP or the next step in the purchase journey, (4) Verify the device configuration selected before login is preserved.
Enhance test case 1436 to add validation steps for authentication completion and redirection under delayed rendering conditions to ensure the flow works correctly even with network latency.

Create negative test cases to validate that: (1) Users cannot proceed to checkout without authentication, (2) Session timeout during authentication returns user to appropriate step with error message, (3) Failed login attempts do not lose user configuration.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC6 – Error Handling (Partially Covered)

The application shall gracefully handle error scenarios including:

Network interruption while loading pages.
Device unavailability or out-of-stock condition.
Slow network response while loading the Product Details Page.
HTTP 500/Internal Server Error.
API timeout while retrieving product details.
Display appropriate error messages without crashing.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify system behavior when navigating to All Phones with network interruption
Verify system behavior when Samsung Galaxy A57 5G device card is not available on listing page
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test case 1432 validates error handling for network interruption while loading pages and ensures the system displays appropriate error messages without crashing. Test case 1433 validates handling of device unavailability or out-of-stock conditions. However, there are no explicit test cases covering HTTP 500/Internal Server Error, API timeout while retrieving product details, or slow network response specifically while loading the Product Details Page. These gaps create risk of poor error handling in production, potentially resulting in application crashes, blank pages, or confusing user experiences during backend failures.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create test case to validate HTTP 500/Internal Server Error handling: (1) Simulate HTTP 500 error when loading PDP, (2) Verify appropriate error message is displayed (e.g., 'We're experiencing technical difficulties. Please try again later.'), (3) Verify application does not crash and user can navigate back or retry, (4) Verify error is logged for monitoring.

Create test case to validate API timeout while retrieving product details: (1) Simulate API timeout (e.g., 30+ seconds) when fetching product details, (2) Verify timeout error message is displayed, (3) Verify loading indicator is removed, (4) Verify user can retry or navigate back.

Create test case to validate slow network response specifically while loading the Product Details Page: (1) Simulate slow network (e.g., 3G connection), (2) Verify loading indicators are displayed, (3) Verify page eventually loads successfully or times out gracefully, (4) Verify user experience remains acceptable with progressive loading.
Implement comprehensive error monitoring and alerting to capture production error scenarios not covered by test cases.

fully_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC1 – Mobile Devices Listing (Fully Covered)

The customer shall be able to:

Navigate from the StarHub Home page to Mobile → All Phones.
View the Mobile Devices listing page.
Verify the page heading is displayed correctly.
Verify the correct URL is loaded.
View all available mobile devices.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify successful navigation to mobile devices listing page from StarHub personal homepage

fully_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion:
AC2 – Product Details Page (Fully Covered)

The customer shall be able to:

Select Samsung Galaxy A57 5G from the device listing.
Navigate to the Product Details Page.
Verify the product information.
Verify the Product Details Page URL.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify successful selection and navigation to Samsung Galaxy A57 5G device details page
